_meta.notes: Curated maritime chokepoints layer for the Global Map. Every share/statistic is quoted from the named source with its year — these are slow-moving structural facts (Chatham House analysis basis 2015-17, updated 2020), not live measurements. Live transit counts exist at IMF PortWatch (linked per chokepoint). quality_flag=curated_sourced throughout; nothing here feeds the FDRS score. v38: added structured transits{commodities,dependents(ISO),risk_vectors,share_note} per chokepoint, all grounded in the cited food_role text (no new unsourced claims), to power the in-app chokepoint analysis.

data.name: Turkish Straits (Bosphorus & Dardanelles)
data.food_role: Gateway for Black Sea grain: ~20% of global wheat exports (Russia, Ukraine, Romania) transit here (Chatham House, 2017 analysis). One of only two food chokepoints with no maritime alternative.
data.recent: Black Sea grain flows remain exposed to the Russia-Ukraine war; the 2022-23 Black Sea Grain Initiative and its collapse showed how closure risk transmits to MENA wheat importers.

data.name: Suez Canal
data.food_role: ~8-9% of global seaborne trade; key southbound leg for Black Sea and European wheat to East Africa, the Gulf and Asia (Chatham House; UNCTAD 2024).
data.recent: 2023-24 Red Sea crisis pushed much of Suez traffic around the Cape of Good Hope, adding ~10-14 days to Europe-Asia food shipments (IMF, Mar 2024).

data.name: Bab el-Mandeb Strait
data.food_role: Red Sea southern gate: the wheat lifeline for Yemen, Sudan, Eritrea and Djibouti — some of the world's most food-insecure import-dependent states — and the Suez-route leg for Gulf food imports (Chatham House).
data.recent: Houthi attacks cut weekly transits ~48% in 2024 (bulk carriers down most), per IMF PortWatch — direct cost inflation on Horn-of-Africa food imports.

data.name: Strait of Hormuz
data.food_role: Sole maritime entry for Gulf food importers (Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, much of UAE/Saudi traffic): ~24 Mt of grain transit annually; no alternative route (Chatham House). The Arabian Peninsula imports nearly all of its food.
data.recent: April 2026 Hormuz tensions (energy crisis reporting, Chatham House) underline the closure scenario the Scenario tab stress-tests for GCC states.

data.name: Strait of Malacca
data.food_role: Largest grain chokepoint by volume: ~108 Mt of grain annually; over a quarter of world soybean exports and ~42% of China's soy imports transit here (Chatham House).
data.recent: Structural congestion risk; alternative routes (Sunda/Lombok) add days and cost for Panamax grain carriers.

data.name: Panama Canal
data.food_role: US Gulf grain's shortcut to Asia: just under three-quarters of Japan's maize and wheat imports and ~34% of China's soy imports transit here (Chatham House).
data.recent: 2023-24 drought cut transit volume ~32% year-on-year (IMF PortWatch) — a climate-driven closure rehearsal for Pacific grain buyers.

data.name: Strait of Gibraltar
data.food_role: Mediterranean gate for Atlantic grain into North Africa (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia wheat imports) and the western leg of the Black Sea-to-MENA wheat route (Chatham House: one of the 8 maritime food chokepoints).
data.recent: Low closure risk; matters as the redundancy route when Suez/Red Sea is disrupted.

data.name: Black Sea ports (Odesa cluster)
data.food_role: Coastal chokepoint: Russia + Ukraine wheat (~19% of world exports, Chatham House) moves 60-65% by rail to these ports before any strait is reached — port closure chokes supply upstream of the Turkish Straits.
data.recent: Repeated strikes and the 2023 Grain Initiative collapse demonstrated single-point failure; Ukrainian exports re-routed via Danube/overland at higher cost.

data.name: Strait of Dover
data.food_role: Europe's densest shipping lane; UK food-import resilience depends on it alongside the short-strait ferry/tunnel corridor (Chatham House: one of the 8 maritime food chokepoints).
data.recent: Operational risk is congestion/weather rather than conflict.
